lines.trans: Alright, Kostya, open your eyes, you can look!
Here, look, I bought the car from Eva!
Wait, Nastya, why did you buy it?
What do you mean why, we are having a baby soon, we cannot manage without a car!
Kostya, are you not happy about the purchase at all?
I am very happy, congratulations on the acquisition!
Would you like us to drive you home today?
No, thank you, then you would have to drive a whole three meters.
Attention everyone in the kitchen, the inspector is coming!
I do not doubt it, only let's make sure everything is fair.
Have all your cooks step out of the kitchen right now!

lines.trans: There are almost no guests in the hall, let them leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Подожди, тут только двадцать пять, а мы на тридцать спорили!
examples.trans: Wait, there is only twenty-five here, and we bet thirty!

examples.text: Смотри, Настя, ещё тридцать тысяч выиграл!
examples.trans: Look, Nastya, I won another thirty thousand!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'metre' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет, спасибо, вам же тогда придётся три метра проехать.
examples.trans: No, thank you, then you would have to drive a whole three meters.

examples.text: Пять метров.
examples.trans: Five metres.

examples.text: Один метр.
examples.trans: One metre.

meanings.en: to get through, to drive past
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drive / ride', paired with 'проезжать'.

examples.text: Нет, спасибо, вам же тогда придётся три метра проехать.
examples.trans: No, thank you, then you would have to drive a whole three meters.

examples.text: Миксер проехать не может.
examples.trans: The mixer truck can't get through.

examples.text: Здесь нельзя проехать.
examples.trans: You can't drive through here.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ребята, прошу внимание всем на минуту!
examples.trans: Folks, may I have everyone's attention for a minute!

examples.text: Внимание всем на кухне, к нам едет ревизор!
examples.trans: Attention everyone in the kitchen, the inspector is coming!

examples.text: Прошу внимания.
examples.trans: May I have your attention.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: Костя, у нас уже двести тысяч набралось.
examples.trans: Kostya, we have already accumulated two hundred thousand.

examples.text: Смотри, если упаду, это будет на твоей совести!
examples.trans: Look, if I fall, it will be on your conscience!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: По поводу ресторана я тебе уже говорил, Дима.
examples.trans: I already told you about the restaurant, Dima.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Что главное в ресторане, конечно кухня и еда!
examples.trans: What is the main thing in a restaurant, the kitchen and food, of course!

examples.text: Главное — кухня и еда!
examples.trans: The main thing is the kitchen and food!

examples.text: Дима, а ты что здесь на кухне делаешь?
examples.trans: Dima, and what are you doing here in the kitchen?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is going (by vehicle)', paired with 'поехать'.

examples.text: Привет, папа, зачем ты сюда приехал?
examples.trans: Hi, Dad, why did you come here?

examples.text: Я приехал поговорить о кафе, которое вы на свадьбу выбрали.
examples.trans: I came to talk about the café that you chose for the wedding.

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна, хорошо, что вы не уехали, вы ключи забыли.
examples.trans: Viktoria Sergeyevna, it is a good thing you did not leave, you forgot your keys.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'inspector' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Внимание всем на кухне, к нам едет ревизор!
examples.trans: Attention everyone in the kitchen, the inspector is coming!

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть ревизор.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always inspector.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'омневаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'doubt', paired with 'усомниться'.

examples.text: Я не сомневаюсь.
examples.trans: I have no doubt.

examples.text: Никто не сомневался.
examples.trans: Nobody doubted it.

examples.text: А никто и не сомневался.
examples.trans: Nobody ever doubted it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я из этого всего только слово кролик знаю!
examples.trans: Out of all those words, I only know the word rabbit!

examples.text: Настя, мне только что премию дали, пятьдесят тысяч!
examples.trans: Nastya, they just gave me a bonus, fifty thousand!

examples.text: Подожди, тут только двадцать пять, а мы на тридцать спорили!
examples.trans: Wait, there is only twenty-five here, and we bet thirty!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: А давай мы с тобой сейчас поспорим!
examples.trans: Let's you and I make a bet right now!

examples.text: Давай мы с тобой поспорим!
examples.trans: Let's you and I make a bet!

examples.text: Давайте снимем хотя бы ваш ресторан, я оплачу всё!
examples.trans: Let's rent at least your restaurant, I will pay for everything!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

examples.text: Да ничего не рухнет, главное в ресторане что?
examples.trans: Nothing will collapse, what is the main thing in a restaurant?

examples.text: Что главное в ресторане, конечно кухня и еда!
examples.trans: What is the main thing in a restaurant, the kitchen and food, of course!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.text: Я просто хочу быть таким же крутым, как ты!
examples.trans: I just want to be as cool as you!

examples.text: Я думаю, может быть, специи не свежие были?
examples.trans: I think maybe the spices were not fresh?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Скажи честно, а тебе это вообще зачем?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, why do you even need this?

examples.text: Не сомневаюсь, только давай, чтобы всё было честно.
examples.trans: I do not doubt it, only let's make sure everything is fair.

examples.text: Хочешь, честно скажу?
examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть сегодня вы от нас уходите, мы будем помнить вас.
examples.trans: Even though you are leaving us today, we will remember you.

examples.text: Ты такую прекрасную женщину упустил, Макс!
examples.trans: You let such a wonderful woman slip away, Max!

examples.text: Пусть сейчас все твои повара выйдут из кухни!
examples.trans: Have all your cooks step out of the kitchen right now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: А давай мы с тобой сейчас поспорим!
examples.trans: Let's you and I make a bet right now!

examples.text: Да нет, мы же сейчас не общаемся.
examples.trans: Well no, we are not speaking right now.

examples.text: Подожди, Дима, я тебя сейчас не понял.
examples.trans: Wait, Dima, I did not understand you just now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Надеюсь, я умру не от твоего блюда!
examples.trans: I hope I do not die from your dish!

examples.text: Значит, она просто удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: That means she simply deleted your number.

examples.text: Она удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: She deleted your number.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cook' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: По поводу ресторана я тебе уже говорил, Дима.
examples.trans: I already told you about the restaurant, Dima.

examples.text: Поверь мне, я знаю, о чём говорю!
examples.trans: Believe me, I know what I am talking about!

examples.text: О, наш повар наконец проснулся!
examples.trans: Oh, our cook has finally woken up!

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

related.gloss: not to to go out (negated infinitive)

examples.text: И примите от коллектива этот красивый букет.
examples.trans: And accept this beautiful bouquet from the team.

examples.text: Красивый букет, это очередной поклонник подарил?
examples.trans: Nice bouquet, did another admirer give it to you?

examples.text: Пусть сейчас все твои повара выйдут из кухни!
examples.trans: Have all your cooks step out of the kitchen right now!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дочка, ты пойми, свадьба — это один раз в жизни.
examples.trans: Sweetheart, understand, a wedding is once in a lifetime.

examples.text: Ну, или максимум два раза в жизни.
examples.trans: Well, or at most twice in a lifetime.

examples.text: Той ерундой, которой ты всю жизнь занимаешься, научи меня!
examples.trans: That nonsense you have been doing your whole life, teach me!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'of the people' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Народа в зале почти нет, пусть выйдут из кухни!
examples.trans: There are almost no guests in the hall, let them leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Народ меня поддерживает.
examples.trans: The people support me.

examples.text: Здесь много народу.
examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Двадцать четыре часа в сутки работаю как раб.
examples.trans: I work twenty-four hours a day like a slave.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hall' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Народа в зале почти нет, пусть выйдут из кухни!
examples.trans: There are almost no guests in the hall, let them leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Прошу в зал суда.
examples.trans: Please enter the courtroom.

examples.text: Большой зал.
examples.trans: A big hall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'almost', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А почему ты нам её не предлагаешь?
examples.trans: And why are you not offering it to us?

examples.text: А всё почему, потому что я настоящий гений!
examples.trans: And why is that, because I am a true genius!

examples.text: Народа в зале почти нет, пусть выйдут из кухни!
examples.trans: There are almost no guests in the hall, let them leave the kitchen!
